text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition to hosting the 2004 Olympics in Stockholm is growing among Swedes with over 52 percent of Swedes against it following the Atlanta games, according to a new Swedish poll.
- The government and the centre party have agreed on a plan to downsize the Swedish regiments, shedding 4,000 jobs.
- The deregulation of Swedish transport has led to lower prices and more travellers using the system, according to the Swedish competition board.

- An unknown elk disease is again spreading throughout Sweden, killing many of the animals. The disease was first discovered 10 years ago and has since killed thousands of elks but no cure has been found.

- Carl Bildt, leader of the Swedish conservative party and former prime minister, is proposing to establish a North European partnership for peace (NPFP) which would unite the Baltic states with four Nordic states in a security network.
- Scania Trucks is launching an environmentally friendly new bus for city areas, Omnicity.
- A British investment fund managed by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, currently under investigation for "possible irregularities", has nearly four billion crowns placed in Scandinavian companies.
- Swedish Saab Military Aircraft, producer of the JAS Gripen fighter, may in the future supply components for the Eurofighter.
- Mail order firm Ellos, the largest clothing mail order company in Sweden, has strengthened its market position by acquiring Josefssons Postorder.
